approach: When the request text names commit hashes, the producer and verifier snapshots get one extra file, ATHENA-COMMITS.txt, at the snapshot root. The core writes it as text from the user's repository. For each named commit that is an ancestor of the base commit it records the full hash, date, subject, visible changed paths and a unified diff limited to visible paths. Visibility uses the same classify() and visible_to_agents() filter as history_text. No real git object, ref, alternate or remote enters the snapshot. The file is listed in the snapshot's .git/info/exclude, so the candidate, the change list and the verifier's prepared tree ignore it. The tokenizer commit_hashes_in lives in athena-context (briefs.rs), so the briefs and the core share one function. athena-git takes a ready list of hashes. The brief sentence is added only when commit_hashes_in(request) is non-empty, so a brief for a request with no hash stays byte-identical and the stored-copy test is unchanged. Revision 3: checks.rs is dropped, because verifier_snapshot keeps its 4-argument form as a wrapper for the scratch demonstration run and a new verifier_snapshot_for(ctx) is used by the three agent-read callers. mod.rs (one line) and run_pin_tests.rs (test only) stay, with reasons. The hidden-name assertions are split. The ripgrep rationale is corrected. A missing request is handled. A blob-hash case is added. The on-main limit is documented.

decisions.choice: Generate a filtered text view in the core and expose no real git objects in the snapshot.
decisions.reason: Real objects reached through alternates, a fetched pack or a remote leak hidden-path blobs and trees through the object database. A generated file reuses the filter history_text uses, and every role reads it with Read. The user's repository is only read.

rejected.option: Alternates or a remote to the user's repository
rejected.why: Gives a path back to records/ and athena-exclude content; criterion 3 and D08 forbid it.

rejected.option: Rewrite the named commits into the snapshot's git
rejected.why: Rewritten commits get new ids, so the cited hash would not resolve; tree surgery across merges risks hidden blobs in the object store.

rejected.option: Always include full history or extend HISTORY.txt

decisions.choice: Exclude the file with /ATHENA-COMMITS.txt in .git/info/exclude, written before the file; copy_files skips that top-level name for a resumed directory. The brief tells agents to Read the file, or Grep it, by its explicit path.
decisions.reason: Candidate and prepared trees come from git add -A (work_tree_tree, commit_all), so an unexcluded file would enter the candidate and break the tree_now == prepared checks (verification.rs:284, 299, 327). Ripgrep honours .git/info/exclude, so a directory-wide Grep will not find the file; a path given explicitly to Read or Grep does. This corrects the earlier rationale (finding 6).

rejected.why: Same hiding from directory-wide search and an unusual path to explain; no gain over the exclude.

rejected.option: Commit it into the snapshot's base commit
rejected.why: Changes the one-commit and two-commit shape and the base tree the change list is measured against.

decisions.choice: Accept a hash only if rev_parse resolves it as a commit and it is an ancestor of the base commit. Everything else, including a commit that changed only hidden paths, goes under one shared note in the file and in CommitViews.omitted. The result is Ok.
decisions.reason: Git::rev_parse already resolves <rev>^{commit} with --verify --quiet (lib.rs:289-296), so a token matching a tree or blob, including a hidden file's blob, resolves to None and goes straight to the note; a test covers it (finding 8). One shared note does not confirm that a hidden commit exists. A typo must not fail the job. D08, the changelog and enforcement.md state that only commits in the base's history are shown, so a commit that is not on main, such as an earlier rejected candidate, gets only the note (finding 9).

rejected.option: Refuse the job on an unknown hash
rejected.why: A mistyped token would stop the job over a convenience feature.
The agent could not tell a missing view from an empty one, which was the fault behind the rejected attempts.

decisions.choice: Put commit_hashes_in(text) -> Vec<String> in athena-context briefs.rs, with COMMITS_FILE. Split on non-alphanumerics, keep 7 to 40 hex characters with at least one digit and one letter, lowercase, deduplicate, keep the first 8. Core callers take the text from ctx.job.request.as_ref().map(|r| r.text.as_str()).unwrap_or(""), the form used at mod.rs:865 and verification.rs:66-71, so a missing request means no hashes and no view (finding 7).
decisions.reason: The brief builders need the same test as the core (conditional sentence), and athena-context and athena-git do not depend on each other; one definition avoids drift and a new dependency. Each candidate is still re-checked by rev_parse, so a false positive costs a note. Digit-only hashes are not detected; the changelog says so.

rejected.option: Tokenizer in athena-git plus a copy in briefs.rs
A regex crate over the whole brief
rejected.why: Adds a dependency and picks up hashes from text the user did not write.

decisions.choice: Make the brief sentence conditional on commit_hashes_in(&inputs.request) being non-empty, with no new field on ProducerInputs or VerifierInputs. The sentence says to Read ATHENA-COMMITS.txt by its path, and that if the file is absent Athena could not build the view.
decisions.reason: The two input structs are built at 63 sites in briefs.rs tests alone; a new field would touch them all. A request-derived condition keeps no-hash briefs byte-identical, including VERIFIER_BRIEF_WITHOUT_A_PLAN (briefs.rs:3600-3621), and the core writes the file exactly when the same list is non-empty and the view succeeded (finding 5).

rejected.option: Unconditional sentence and an updated stored copy
rejected.why: Points agents at a file that does not exist and changes every brief.

rejected.option: A boolean field on the input structs
rejected.why: Edits dozens of unrelated test literals.

decisions.choice: One file, with the subject only (no body, no author). Cap each diff at 200 KB with a visible truncation line. At most 8 commits.
decisions.reason: Mirrors HISTORY.txt. A body can name hidden paths, and an author is personal data.

rejected.why: More paths to explain and more name collisions.

decisions.choice: Keep verifier_snapshot(dir, base, candidate, pin_dir) unchanged in signature as a wrapper with no view. Add verifier_snapshot_for(dir, base, candidate, ctx) in verification.rs. Both call one private builder that takes the hash list. Switch mod.rs:1502 and verification.rs:298 and :326 to the _for form. Leave checks.rs:367 untouched.
decisions.reason: checks.rs:367 builds a scratch snapshot where demonstration commands run (reverted files written at lines 379-384); no agent reads it, so it needs no view. The call at mod.rs:1502 is the main verifier snapshot and sits in mod.rs, so a one-line edit there is forced; the only alternative is hidden shared state. This drops checks.rs from the plan (finding 2) and keeps mod.rs to one line (finding 1).

rejected.option: Change the signature for all callers
rejected.why: Forces an edit to checks.rs for no behavior.

rejected.option: Stash the hashes in a field on Athena
rejected.why: Shared state that every caller must keep in step.

decisions.choice: Keep the core wiring test in crates/athena-core/src/run_pin_tests.rs.
decisions.reason: It is a test-only file (mod run_pin_tests, lib.rs:109) and holds the fake-invoker harness that records spec.workdir for the producer and the verifier (lines 866 and 933). It is the only place to show the wiring in producer.rs and verification.rs. Without it the wiring has no behavior evidence, which the behavior-evidence default rejects (finding 3).

rejected.option: A new harness in producer.rs or verification.rs
rejected.why: Duplicates the fake invoker and RunContext set-up.

decisions.choice: Do not edit docs/system-facts.md; raise its stale producer-snapshot line as a question.
decisions.reason: It is not a listed deliverable.

risks.risk: A hidden path name or content leaks through the diff (rename, submodule line, textconv or external diff driver from the user's .gitattributes).
risks.mitigation: Paths come from diff_tree with --no-renames, are filtered by classify() and passed as literal pathspecs; --no-ext-diff and --no-textconv are set; mode 160000 entries are dropped; the body and author are never written. Criterion 2 checks file bytes and git output, with the unfiltered control.

risks.risk: A visible .gitattributes, or a requested commit that edits it, still names the paths it hides.
risks.mitigation: This matches today's snapshots. The criterion 2 assertions are scoped (finding 4), and D08 and enforcement.md state the limit.

risks.risk: The view file leaks into the candidate commit or changes the verifier's prepared tree, so a verdict would be discarded and rerun.
risks.mitigation: The path goes into .git/info/exclude before the file is written. Tests compare work_tree_tree() before and after and check the candidate's tree in the core test.

risks.risk: Directory-wide Grep skips the excluded file, so an agent may not find it.
risks.mitigation: The brief sentence names the file and says to Read it or Grep it by its explicit path; the brief test asserts the wording.

risks.risk: A real tracked file already named ATHENA-COMMITS.txt, or a view error, leaves the brief pointing at a missing file.
risks.mitigation: add_commit_views returns Refused rather than overwrite; the core prints a warning and the job continues. The brief sentence says that an absent file means Athena could not build the view.

risks.risk: Huge commits make the file very large.
risks.mitigation: At most 8 commits and 200 KB of diff per commit with a visible truncation line; the path list is always complete.

risks.risk: Missed or false hash detection in the request text.
risks.mitigation: The matcher is conservative and tested on dates, job ids, versions and all-hex words; every candidate is checked with rev_parse; a miss leaves today's behavior, stated in the changelog.

risks.risk: A cited commit that is not on the base's history (an earlier rejected candidate) shows only the note.
risks.mitigation: Stated in D08 and the changelog; a note explains why nothing is shown.

risks.risk: The core wiring test depends on a harness read only by grep so far.
risks.mitigation: Step 6 reads it before the test is written; if it cannot expose both workdirs, the test records them through the same fake invoker at the two snapshot builders.

demonstrations.method: athena-git unit test. Build user_repo() plus a later commit that adds src/feature.rs and edits src/main.rs. Call Snapshot::create(.., SnapshotRepo::Base), then snap.add_commit_views(&git, &head, &head, &[full hash of the extra commit]). Read ATHENA-COMMITS.txt from the snapshot dir. A second case uses the 7-character abbreviation.
demonstrations.observes: The file holds the full hash, date, subject, the paths src/feature.rs and src/main.rs, '+++ b/src/feature.rs' and an added source line; CommitViews.shown holds the full hash and omitted is empty.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without add_commit_views writing the view, the file is missing and the read fails; the test does not compile against the pre-change crate.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points Snapshot::create (exists, snapshot.rs:59) and Snapshot::add_commit_views (added by plan step 2). Fixture: real temporary git repositories from testutil::repo_with and commit_all (exist), passed as the user: &Git argument. No double.

demonstrations.method: athena-git unit test. The requested commit changes src/main.rs (visible), FRONT.md (hidden by the visible root .gitattributes), private/notes.md (hidden by private/.gitattributes; the whole private/ directory is absent from snapshots, snapshot.rs:534) and records/jobs/y.json, each hidden file holding a unique marker. Create Base and BaseAndCandidate snapshots, add the view, then read every file under the snapshot dir including .git, and run `git log --all -p` and `git cat-file --batch-all-objects --batch` through snap.git(). Split assertions. (a) No marker content appears in any file or git output. (b) The names private/notes.md, records/jobs/y.json and records/ appear in no file and no git output, since no visible file names them. (c) The name FRONT.md is asserted absent from ATHENA-COMMITS.txt only, because the visible root .gitattributes (and its blob in the snapshot's base commit) legitimately names it, as today's snapshots already do. (d) A case where the requested commit edits .gitattributes asserts that the visible diff is shown and names the paths it hides; this is documented in D08 and enforcement.md. (e) HISTORY.txt from a PlainWithHistory snapshot omits the hidden paths. (f) A commit that touched only hidden paths is under the 'not available' note and its subject is absent. The control first computes an unfiltered `git show` of the commit in the user repo and runs the same assertion set on it; the markers and names are found there, so the assertions can fail.
demonstrations.observes: No hidden content or hidden name outside the allowed .gitattributes lines, while the visible part of the same commit is present, so the test is not vacuous.
demonstrations.fails_without: With an unfiltered git show as the diff, the markers and names appear in the file and (a), (b) and (c) fail; the control shows the content is reachable without the filter.
demonstrations.seam: Snapshot::create (exists) and Snapshot::add_commit_views (step 2). Fixture: a user_repo()-style temporary repository with .gitattributes exclude rules, passed as user. The real classify() (attrs.rs:46) runs; nothing is stubbed.

The existing snapshot_git_cannot_reach_the_users_history_or_hidden_content (snapshot.rs:555) stays.

demonstrations.method: Content check plus a brief test. docs/enforcement.md gains a paragraph under the snapshot-isolation rows: what the view holds, what stays hidden (records/, athena-exclude paths, commit bodies and authors, commits outside the base's history), the mechanism (classify() filter, no alternates or remote) and the tests. CHANGELOG.md gets an Added entry under Unreleased for outside readers with the limits: request text only, at most 8 hashes, digit-only hashes not detected, a commit not on the base's history (for example an earlier rejected candidate) shows only a note. The producer 'Working directory' text (briefs.rs:451, 460, both forms) and the verifier 'The change' text (briefs.rs:1187) gain one conditional sentence after 'history are absent by design', so the assertions at 2717 and 3612 still hold when no hash is named. The brief test asserts the file name and that the file is read by its path in the producer plain form, the retry form and the verifier brief for a request naming a hash, and asserts the sentence is absent for a request with none.
demonstrations.observes: The file name and the 'by its path' wording are found in all three brief forms when a hash is named, and in none otherwise. The doc diffs are checked by reading.
